tasks.short: Set advertising strategy, approve campaign plans, coordinate execution, and adjust activity using results.

steps.what: Gather campaign results, spend, customer responses, and commercial targets.
Summarise previous lessons and draft strategic options.

loop.input: Campaign baseline, brand guidelines, and approved campaign reviews.
loop.output: Source-linked strategy options with assumptions and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Trace figures to the baseline; distinguish observations from hypotheses; manager checks commercial relevance.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per planning round; missing evidence stays flagged for manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates organise the pack, but interpreting narrative lessons and proposing options needs language judgement.

steps.what: Agree audience priorities, positioning, channel choices, and acceptable tradeoffs.
Write advertising policies, campaign briefs, and measurement requirements.

loop.input: Recorded strategy decisions, approved templates, brand guidelines, and budget envelope.
loop.output: Draft policy, campaign brief, and measurement plan.
loop.check: Validate required fields and budget arithmetic; manager checks fidelity to decisions and supported claims.
loop.stop: One draft and two targeted revisions; unresolved policy questions return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed fields are deterministic, but translating decisions into clear policy and briefs needs bounded drafting.

steps.what: Approve policy, campaign scope, spending limits, and exceptions.
Configure audiences, schedules, budgets, and placements, then launch approved campaigns.
Review early results and decide whether to change the campaign.

tasks.design: Configure feeds from the {ADS}, {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}, {CRM}, and {ERP} into a campaign baseline in the {BI}; bounded drafting loops turn approved evidence and recorded decisions into planning documents in the {DOCS}. The {WORKFLOW} routes approvals and prepares campaign settings, with a human approving the exact audience, assets, budget, and schedule before launch. Deterministic checks enforce contact permissions, suppression lists, and spending limits.
tasks.previous_blocker: Channel definitions, finance figures, and narrative lessons were disconnected. Existing reporting tools could collect numbers, but strategy choices and approvals still needed people.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing connectors and approval features handle much of the flow. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building mapping rules, validators, and template generators; bounded drafting helps with narrative material.
tasks.still_hard: Attribution remains uncertain. Positioning, competing commercial priorities, novel claims, and unusual channel restrictions need judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a defensible position, challenge misleading results, and negotiate tradeoffs between growth, customer trust, and spending.

ambition.what: A fortnightly channel experiment decision using a consistent evidence pack.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less evidence assembly and document rewriting, leaving more time for experiments and creative direction. The manager can propose more frequent changes; existing spending and publication rights remain.

reach.role: Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists
reach.task: Design a campaign experiment that separates response changes from audience differences.
reach.learn: Sampling, comparison groups, uncertainty, and the limits of channel attribution.

evidence.claim: Funnel offers channel-data connectors, standardisation, and automated marketing reporting.
HubSpot offers campaign planning and branded-content generation; this supports drafting capability, not autonomous strategic judgement.
Spotler supports marketing journeys and campaign-data queries.
Electronic marketing and non-essential tracking have consent requirements and applicable exceptions.
An objection to direct marketing requires that processing for that purpose stop, including related profiling.
The proposed decomposition, remaining-time estimates, and pilot build ranges are design estimates.

assumptions: The pilot covers one campaign team and its main channels.
Standard connectors or supported exports are available; build ranges are working-day estimates, not elapsed delivery promises.
Brand policy, budget ownership, and campaign approval roles already exist.
GDPR and EU AI Act obligations apply; transparency and disclosure requirements are assessed for the actual content and use.
National rules determine any employee consultation required by changed workflows; the design does not score employees.
unknowns: Which channel connectors and approval features are licensed.
Whether spend and response records share reliable campaign identifiers.
Who can approve launches and budget changes.
Which contact permissions and tracking choices are recorded.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for this rollout.
research_questions: Which current reporting fields reconcile reliably with finance totals?
Which campaign settings can be staged and previewed before publication?
What comparison method would make the first channel experiment useful?
new_work: Review source-linked drafts and unsupported assumptions.
Resolve missing identifiers and discrepancies between channel and finance data.
Maintain campaign templates, permission checks, and connector mappings.
Review launch previews and investigate failed or partial launches.

tasks.short: Find suitable promotional contacts, make introductions, and develop relationships around shared campaign opportunities.

steps.what: Agree target buyers, partner profiles, and the proposed promotional offer.
Filter existing contacts and reconcile duplicate or incomplete records.
Research contact roles, audience fit, and relevant industry activity.

loop.input: A fixed set of permitted directory entries, partner materials, and contact records.
loop.output: Contact dossiers with source dates, roles, audience evidence, and missing facts.
loop.check: Require a source for each extracted fact; distinguish organisation facts from individual details; review uncertain identities.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per dossier; missing or conflicting facts enter an exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Role descriptions and audience evidence appear in varied prose that fixed field mappings cannot reliably parse.

steps.what: Choose contacts and decide the introduction route.
Write and send a personal introduction or promotional invitation.

loop.input: Approved offer, verified contact dossier, introduction plan, and permitted relationship history.
loop.output: A short introduction draft using supported facts.
loop.check: Validate recipient eligibility and suppression status deterministically; manager approves recipient, wording, and any commitment before sending.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per selected contact; uncertain eligibility blocks sending and returns to a person.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed template cannot adequately express varied relationship context and a relevant personal introduction.

steps.what: Explore shared interests, build trust, and agree a possible collaboration.
Record relationship status, agreed actions, and follow-up dates.

tasks.design: Configure contact filtering, duplicate checks, structured meeting outcomes, and follow-up tasks in the {CRM}; a bounded extraction loop prepares source-linked dossiers from permitted material in the {DOCS}. A bounded drafting loop prepares introductions, while the {WORKFLOW} checks contact permissions and suppression before a manager approves sending through the {EMAIL}. Relationship conversations stay with the manager, with agreed actions captured once.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relationship context was dispersed across personal mailboxes, contact records, and informal introductions. Contact filtering already existed, but source verification and personalised preparation took effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Configurable contact records and follow-up rules can handle the structured work. Small extraction and drafting loops can process varied prose without delegating relationship ownership.
tasks.still_hard: Public information becomes stale, identities are ambiguous, and a relevant contact may have no interest or authority. Trust and permission to communicate cannot be inferred from a directory entry.
tasks.human_edge: Earn introductions, recognise mutual benefit, and sense when pursuing a contact would damage the relationship.

ambition.what: A quarterly promotional partnership programme for small regional distributors.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling dossiers and updating records, and more time on selected partner conversations. Authority to make commercial commitments remains within existing limits.

reach.task: Prepare a stakeholder relationship map for a promotional partnership.
reach.learn: Stakeholder interests, introduction etiquette, source verification, and relationship-sensitive communication.

evidence.claim: Spotler offers lead management and marketing journeys, supporting the structured contact-workflow component.
HubSpot offers prospecting outreach generation; the proposed design retains approval before sending.
Electronic direct marketing is subject to consent requirements, applicable exceptions, and national implementation rules.
Direct-marketing objections must stop the relevant processing.
Dossier extraction, time estimates, and build ranges are proposed pilot designs, not documented relationship-development outcomes.

assumptions: The pilot uses existing contact records and a fixed set of permitted research sources.
Structured meeting outcomes replace repeated entry of the same relationship information.
GDPR applies to identifiable business contacts; contact availability alone does not establish marketing eligibility.
National rules determine channel-specific marketing requirements and any employee consultation needed for mailbox integration.
Build ranges cover one team and exclude purchasing new research datasets.
unknowns: Whether contact records include reliable roles, source dates, permissions, and objections.
Which research sources permit the intended use.
Which mailboxes the team may connect and what access restrictions apply.
Who can approve partner offers and commercial commitments.
Whether the proposed distributor group has a viable shared offer.
research_questions: Which dossier fields change the manager's contact-selection decision?
How often do record collisions require human identity checks?
Which introduction routes produce useful conversations without excessive follow-up?
new_work: Review uncertain identities, stale facts, and missing source dates.
Approve personalised introductions and resolve eligibility exceptions.
Maintain duplicate rules, retention settings, and suppression synchronisation.
Keep structured relationship outcomes current after conversations.

tasks.short: Coach advertising staff, assign production work, and review creative quality.

steps.what: Review recent advertisements, revisions, and recurring production problems.

loop.input: Selected advertisement samples, revision notes, and an approved issue taxonomy.
loop.output: Source-linked production issues grouped by issue type, without employee rankings.
loop.check: Manager verifies examples and context; deterministic checks handle dimensions, required fields, and file versions.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one repair per sample batch; ambiguous creative judgements remain unclassified.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text revision notes describe similar production issues in different language.

steps.what: Discuss learning needs and diagnose whether problems concern skills, briefs, or workload.
Assemble training examples, exercises, and production checklists.
Teach techniques, demonstrate revisions, and coach staff through exercises.
Assign production work, deadlines, and review responsibilities.
Review revised advertisements and give specific creative feedback.
Record training attendance and completed learning activities.

tasks.design: A bounded loop groups revision notes from the {DOCS} and {PROJECT} into source-linked production issues for a manager to review. A deterministic generator assembles selected modules and examples into training packs, while the {PROJECT} prepares assignment templates and the {LMS} records completion. Coaching and creative judgement stay human, with approval before assignments become active or work passes the production review.
tasks.previous_blocker: Creative examples and coaching material were scattered, while preparation depended on the manager's memory. Assignment and learning features existed, but their connection to production work was weak.
tasks.enabler_now: Simple generators can assemble approved learning material, and existing workflow features can handle assignments and completion records. A bounded classifier can organise narrative revision notes.
tasks.still_hard: An error may come from a poor brief, workload, missing skills, or a deliberate creative choice. Staff development depends on candid discussion and fair interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: Give feedback that improves craft without undermining confidence, and distinguish a learning need from a management problem.

ambition.what: A monthly creative craft clinic using approved examples from recent campaigns.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling materials and recording attendance, and more time coaching and clarifying briefs. Staffing, development, and creative approval rights remain with the existing managers.

reach.task: Create annotated examples that explain why an advertisement's visual hierarchy works.
reach.learn: Visual hierarchy, accessibility, production constraints, and constructive design critique.

evidence.claim: Template-based learning packs, assignment workflows, and completion recording are established software patterns.
The digest provides no documented case for automating advertising staff coaching or creative supervision.
The proposed issue classifier, remaining-time estimates, and build ranges require pilot validation.
GDPR, applicable EU AI Act requirements, and national employment and consultation rules affect employee-data workflows.

assumptions: Approved learning modules and reusable creative examples exist.
The issue summary concerns production artefacts and does not rank employees or recommend personnel decisions.
Managers select coaching priorities and assignments using direct discussion and ordinary workload information.
Employee-data access, retention, consultation, and the actual AI use classification are reviewed before rollout under EU law and national rules.
Build ranges cover one creative team; required consultation may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Whether revision notes are retained in an accessible, consistent location.
Whether examples contain confidential client or employee information.
Which approved learning modules are reusable.
Which employee representatives must be consulted under national rules.
Whether the existing learning system can accept completion events.
research_questions: Can reviewers reliably separate production defects from subjective creative preferences?
Which recurring issues merit a checklist rather than a training session?
Does the generated pack help staff improve work without increasing review overhead?
new_work: Verify issue classifications and remove misleading examples.
Maintain approved modules, examples, and production checklists.
Correct completion-record errors and maintain employee-data access boundaries.

tasks.short: Prepare launch presentations, demonstrate products, answer questions, and support field staff and customers.

steps.what: Collect approved product facts, launch assets, and current demonstration instructions.
Adapt the presentation and demonstration sequence to the audience.

loop.input: Versioned launch source pack, audience brief, and approved presentation template.
loop.output: Audience-specific slides, speaker notes, and a proposed demo sequence.
loop.check: Link product claims to approved facts; validate required sections; manager checks slide rendering, audience fit, and demo feasibility.
loop.stop: One draft and two revisions per audience pack; unsupported claims and unavailable features are excluded.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates can place facts, but audience-specific explanations and transitions require bounded language drafting.

steps.what: Rehearse the demonstration and approve the presentation for use.
Confirm participants, timing, venue, and technical requirements.
Present the launch and demonstrate the product or service to participants.
Answer situational questions and identify issues requiring specialist follow-up.
Send promised materials and route unanswered questions to specialists.

loop.input: Structured follow-up commitments, unresolved questions, approved materials, and participant list.
loop.output: Follow-up message draft and proposed specialist routing.
loop.check: Match attachments and recipients to commitments; verify dates and claims; manager approves the outgoing message.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per session; uncertain answers remain unanswered and route to a specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Session-specific questions and commitments need concise contextual wording; recipient and attachment checks remain deterministic.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} collects versioned launch material from the {DOCS} and {PROJECT}, then a bounded generator fills approved presentation templates and drafts audience-specific notes. The manager rehearses using the product demonstration environment recorded under {OTHER}, approves the presentation, and delivers the live session. The {CALENDAR} handles scheduling, while a bounded follow-up draft and deterministic routing connect unanswered questions to specialists through the {EMAIL} and {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Launch material changed across several files, and audience adaptations required manual editing. Most of the task was already live interaction, which preparation tools could not replace.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned source packs, document templates, and scheduling workflows can remove preparation friction. Bounded drafting can adapt approved facts without being allowed to invent product capabilities.
tasks.still_hard: Demonstrations fail, participants ask unexpected questions, and customer needs differ. Confident delivery and honest handling of uncertainty remain situational skills.
tasks.human_edge: Read the room, demonstrate credibly, and acknowledge limits while maintaining customer confidence.

ambition.what: A launch demonstration clinic for regional field staff who cannot attend the main launch.

tasks.altitude: Live demonstrations and questions still dominate the week; preparation and follow-up become shorter. The manager can offer additional small-group sessions, with no automatic change to product-claim or commercial authority.

reach.task: Turn recurring launch questions into an approved demonstration guide.
reach.learn: Task-based explanation, product-version control, technical verification, and clear handling of limitations.

evidence.claim: HubSpot offers branded-content generation, supporting the drafting component but not verified live product demonstrations.
A DHL eCommerce vendor case reports customer-event registration through Spotler Events; it supports event administration, not presentation quality.
Unsupported automatic answers can cause reputational harm; the digest documents DPD disabling an AI chatbot element after abusive responses.
Applicable AI Act transparency obligations depend on the use, including AI interaction and certain synthetic content.
The proposed preparation workflow, remaining-time estimates, and build ranges are pilot estimates.

assumptions: A product owner maintains approved facts and release status.
OTHER denotes a product demonstration environment; its category is not covered by another slot.
The pilot generates presentation files and supports a human presenter.
GDPR governs participant details; recording is outside this pilot.
Applicable EU AI Act disclosure requirements are checked for generated media, and national rules determine any employee consultation needed.
Build ranges cover one launch, one presentation template, and supported document formats.
unknowns: Who approves product facts, claims, and release availability.
Whether demonstration environments support safe rehearsal.
Which presentation formats render reliably in the team's delivery setup.
Which participant details may be retained and reused.
Who owns unanswered technical questions and response deadlines.
research_questions: Which audience adaptations improve comprehension without changing approved claims?
Which demo failures need a prepared fallback sequence?
Which repeated questions justify a new approved guide or specialist session?
new_work: Review generated slides, speaker notes, and rendered layout.
Maintain source-pack versions and invalidate outdated presentations.
Check demonstration readiness and fallback materials.
Approve follow-up messages and track unanswered questions to closure.

role.altitude: The role shifts preparation, reconciliation, and routine coordination into configured workflows and small generators. More time goes to positioning, creative coaching, partnerships, and live persuasion; strategic, staffing, spending, and external-commitment rights remain with their existing owners.
reach: Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists: design useful campaign comparisons and interpret uncertainty.
Public Relations Specialists: map stakeholders and develop relationship-sensitive introductions.
Graphic Designers: explain creative choices through annotated examples.
Technical Writers: turn launch questions into clear, verified guidance.
skills_to_grow: Campaign experiment design and attribution limits.
Writing clear briefs and maintaining approved product facts.
Reviewing source-linked drafts and detecting unsupported claims.
Configuring approvals, contact permissions, and exception queues.
role.ambitious_version: Run a recurring campaign learning programme that links fortnightly experiment decisions, monthly creative clinics, regional distributor partnerships, and field-staff launch clinics. Each service uses shared evidence and approved materials, with people retaining relationship and commercial judgement.
